tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: PowerShell 7+ (pwsh)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` ARE available and work like bash. Prefer `cmd1 && cmd2` over `cmd1; cmd2` when cmd2 should only run if cmd1 succeeds.
   - Ternary (`$cond ? $a : $b`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are available.
   - Default file encoding is UTF-8 without BOM.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name

- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

# Collapses exact duplicates (every column but id) to one row, keeping the
# lowest id. Mirrors the dedupe view the application reads through: the raw
# table and the seed are never modified.
DEDUP_VIEW = """
CREATE VIEW activity_events_dedup AS
SELECT MIN(id) AS id, account_id, location, event_type, occurred_at,
       duration_seconds, outcome
FROM activity_events
GROUP BY account_id, location, event_type, occurred_at,
         duration_seconds, outcome
"""


def load_db(db_dir: Path) -> sqlite3.Connection:
    """Execute schema.sql then seed.sql against a fresh in-memory database."""
    conn = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    for name in ("schema.sql", "seed.sql"):
        path = db_dir / name
        if not path.exists():
            sys.exit(f"missing {path}")
        conn.executescript(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    conn.executescript(DEDUP_VIEW)
    conn.commit()
    return conn


def parse_ts(raw: str) -> datetime:
    """Parse a seed timestamp as UTC. Seeds use 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS'."""
    return datetime.fromisoformat(raw.strip()).replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)


def week_start(d: date) -> date:
    """Monday of the ISO week containing d."""
    return d - timedelta(days=d.weekday())


def iter_weeks(first: date, last: date):
    """Yield every Monday from the week of first through the week of last."""
    cur = week_start(first)
    end = week_start(last)
    while cur <= end:
        yield cur
        cur += timedelta(days=7)


class Window:
    """An account's observation window in its own local calendar.

    A Mon-Sun bucket is COMPLETE only when all seven of its days fall inside
    the window. Completeness is a property of the window, not of where events

Red, as requested: **48 of the new tests fail** with `NotImplementedException`. The other 22 pass: the existing T0–T1 time tests, plus `Thresholds_MatchPlan`, which passes because the stub already declares the three constants.

The Core stubs only have signatures, so the suite compiles. The tests are in `tests/RelayPulse.Tests/Statistics/`:

| File | What it covers |
|---|---|
| `PoissonTailTests` | Tail values checked against an independent Python calculation up to λ=500 (to 1e-9 relative); `P(X≤n) + P(X≥n+1) = 1`; λ=0 and invalid λ; 880 vs 72.3 gives a tail near zero, not NaN |
| `BaselineTests` | Account 6 before 2026-06-08 gives **72.3** (plain mean **138.0**); 7 weeks gives insufficient history; 8 weeks drops the extremes and averages 6; only the last 12 weeks count; ties drop exactly one; 12 zero weeks give λ=0, not null |
| `BandTests` | Your four golden bands plus account 8 (λ=10.4 → [5,20]); lo≥0 and hi≥lo for λ 0.1–500 in 0.1 steps; the band edges match `Assess` (lo and hi are Normal, hi+1 is Above, lo−1 is Below) |
| `AssessTests` | Gate at 3.69 vs 3.70; account 8 is Normal; account 6's spike is Above; the RankKey formula; every flagged row sorts ahead of every unflagged row, across all five verdicts |

All your goldens reproduced independently in Python (log-space tail sums over the dedupe view, account-local weeks). One precision point: the n=0 threshold is exactly ln 40 = **3.6889**, so at λ=3.69 the tail is already below α (e^−3.69 = 0.02497). The tests therefore check the tail at 3.68 vs 3.69, and the verdict at 3.69 (NotEnoughVolume, below the gate) vs 3.70 (Below).

Two implementation choices are baked into the tests:
- **`Upper` sums the upper tail directly when n > λ** instead of computing `1 − Lower(n−1)`. The result is mathematically the same, but the subtraction loses most of its digits far out in the tail (for example, `Upper(600, 500) ≈ 7.8e-6`).
- **NotEnoughVolume and InsufficientHistory get `RankKey = +∞`.** Without that, λ=3 with n=9 would have a key of 0.76 and sort among the flagged rows.

**This spec departs from `CLAUDE.md` and `PLAN.md` §1.** They specify a symmetric quasi-Poisson band `λ ± 2.576·√(φλ)` with φ clamped to [1,4], a gate at λ=3, and a baseline that excludes detected anomaly weeks. Your spec uses exact asymmetric tails, a gate at 3.7, a trimmed mean, and no φ. I'm following your spec. Once it's green I'll log it as REDIRECTED in `ai-log/decisions.md` and update the Statistics rules in `CLAUDE.md`, which would otherwise contradict the code. If you want φ kept for later, say so and I'll note it as deferred instead of dropped.

Should I go ahead with the implementation?

I haven't been able to build, test or run part 2. The shell safety check has returned no verdict eight times in a row, and two more failures would end the turn, so I've stopped retrying.

**Part 1 is done:** 70/70 tests passed on the last run. `PoissonTail`, `Baseline`, `Significance` (band and assess), `Verdict` and `Assessment` are in `src/RelayPulse.Core/Statistics/`.

**Part 2 is written but none of it has been compiled or run:**
- **Core, `Pulse/PulseBuilder`**: pure logic with 10 unit tests in `tests/RelayPulse.Tests/Pulse/PulseBuilderTests.cs`. It zero-fills every (location, complete week) up to the target and never reads partial weeks or weeks after the target. It judges each series against the trimmed baseline and ranks by RankKey, breaking ties by location name. It splits counts by type and outcome, with NULL outcomes keyed as `unspecified`. An account with no events comes back as `insufficient_history`, not λ=0.
- **Api, `Pulse/PulseQuery`**: one parameterised `SqlQueryRaw` over `activity_events_dedup`, range-joined to the complete `week_buckets` rows for the account's timezone. `GROUPING SETS` returns the location and account grains together. It only fetches the 12 baseline weeks plus the target.
- **Api, `Pulse/PulseEndpoints`**: `GET /api/accounts/{id}/pulse?week=`. The default week is the last complete bucket, which comes from the global data cutoff, not the clock. A malformed week, or one that isn't a complete Monday, gets a 400 with title `pulse.invalid_week`. An unknown account gets a 404 with `pulse.account_not_found`. # Relay Pulse — DASH-247

Dashboard feature answering "is this activity normal for us?" per account and per location.
Full reasoning in `PLAN.md`. Data evidence in `tools/profile_seed.py`. This file is the
short version: the rules that must hold in code.

## Status

T0–T1 done: skeleton, SQL Server compose, timezone gate green; EF migrations (accounts,
activity_events, `activity_events_dedup` view, week_buckets), seed import, Core bucket generator.
DB counts match the goldens. Review-state table deferred to T5. Next is T2 (aggregation + `/pulse`).

## Stack

| Layer | Choice |
|---|---|
| Backend | .NET 10 Web API, EF Core 10 (migrations — never `EnsureCreated`) |
| DB | SQL Server in Docker |
| Reads | Raw parameterised SQL via `Database.SqlQueryRaw<T>` for the aggregation; EF for writes |
| Frontend | Angular 21 standalone components + signals. **No NgRx** |
| Tests | xUnit; Testcontainers for integration only |
| Tooling | Python 3.10 — `tools/profile_seed.py` (the data oracle) |

## Structure conventions

- **Solution**: `RelayPulse.slnx` with `src/` (Api, Core) and `tests/` (Tests) solution folders. Three
  projects only.
- **Build**: `Directory.Build.props` sets `net10.0`, `Nullable`, `ImplicitUsings`,
  `TreatWarningsAsErrors` once. No per-csproj duplicates, no `LangVersion` pin.
- **Packages**: central management in `Directory.Packages.props`; EF Core / AspNetCore on 10.0.x,
  `Testcontainers.MsSql` for integration. No `Version=` on a `PackageReference`.
- **DI**: each project exposes one `IServiceCollection` extension (`AddCore()`, …) and `Program.cs`
  composes them. `IClock`'s real implementation is registered there and nowhere else.
- **Async**: every async method takes and passes a `CancellationToken`, down to `SqlQueryRaw`.
- **Errors**: 4xx responses are ProblemDetails with a machine-readable code as `title`
  (e.g. `pulse.invalid_week`). 400 for bad parameters only; an empty account is 200, never 404.
- **Logging**: structured message templates with a `Pulse:` prefix
  (`"Pulse: served {AccountId} week {Week}"`) — never string interpolation.
- **Tests**: xUnit v3, plain `Assert` (no FluentAssertions). API tests go through
  `WebApplicationFactory` and assert on the wire JSON via `JsonElement`. Names are
  `Method_Condition_Outcome`. `Program.cs` ends with `public partial class Program;`.
- **Compose**: SQL Server service has a healthcheck; the API `depends_on` it with
  `condition: service_healthy`.

Rejected alternatives (MediatR, extra layers, versioning, Serilog, …) and their reasons are in
`ai-log/decisions.md`. `C:\src\demos\VerusLLC` was a one-time reference for T0 — do not consult it
again; this file is the source of truth.

## Working rules

**Never read `db/seed.sql` in full.** 2.4MB, ~12,600 INSERTs. It will blow out context and tell
you nothing a query won't. To inspect data, run `python tools/profile_seed.py [--dedupe]`, or
load `schema.sql` + `seed.sql` into in-memory SQLite and query it (see `load_db()` in that file).
`head`/`grep` on it is fine.

**Never edit `db/seed.sql` or `db/schema.sql`.** They are the fixture. Dedupe and reshape happen
in migrations and views, never by rewriting the seed.

**No `DateTime.UtcNow` / `DateTime.Now` / `Date.now()` in domain, query, or view code.** Two
separate reasons, both load-bearing:
- *Correctness*: the dataset ends `2026-07-27`, roughly two months before wall clock. Anything
  keyed off the system clock computes an empty current week. The current period comes from
  `MAX(occurred_at)`, not from now.
- *Testability*: golden-value tests must be stable forever.

Inject an `IClock` where a real timestamp is genuinely needed (review-state `created_at`), and
derive every reporting period from the data. A grep for `UtcNow` outside composition root and
clock implementation should return nothing.

**Tests assert golden values produced by `tools/profile_seed.py --dedupe`** — an independent
implementation, in another language, written before any app code. Do not "fix" a failing test by
copying what the C# returned; re-derive from the profiler and find out which one is wrong.

**Unit tests run with zero infrastructure.** Bucketing, bands, verdicts and window completeness
must not need Docker. Integration tests use Testcontainers and skip with a clear message when
Docker is absent, so `dotnet test` is green either way.

**Log decisions in `ai-log/decisions.md`.** Format is at the top of that file: times in
America/Bogota, `time · ACCEPTED|REJECTED|REDIRECTED · what · why · ref`.

## Domain rules

These come from profiling the seed. Violating one produces plausible, wrong numbers.

**Time**
- `occurred_at` is UTC. Bucket in the **account's own IANA timezone**, Mon–Sun weeks.
- Never bucket in UTC. 8 events land in a different week under UTC — small, and exactly the
  regression that will otherwise ship silently.
- Six zones in play, including `America/Phoenix` (no DST) and a literal `UTC`.
- A week is **complete** only when all 7 days fall inside the observation window. Completeness is
  a property of the window, not of where events land — a week with zero events can be complete.
- **Partial weeks are never compared, never used in a baseline, and never the default view.**
  Both edge buckets (`2026-01-26`, `2026-07-27`) cover 1/7 days for all 20 accounts.
- Default view is the **last complete week**: `2026-07-20 … 2026-07-26`.

**Identity**
- Location key is `(account_id, location)`. Labels are generic (`Site A`…`Site O`) and reused
  across accounts — account 1's Site A is not account 6's Site A.
- `accounts.created_at` is **not** the start of history. Every account's events start `2026-02-01`
  regardless. Never window on `created_at`.
- One timezone per account; the schema cannot express per-location zones (known limitation).

**Reads**
- Raw-SQL result rows must not carry `DateTime` unless mapped: the UTC converter reaches
  `SqlQueryRaw<DateTime>` scalars (via `DefaultTypeMapping`) but **not** `DateTime` members of an
  unmapped record — those come back `Unspecified`. Use `DateOnly`/scalars, or map the row type keyless.
- All reporting reads go through the **dedupe view**, never the raw table. 12 exact duplicate rows
  (7 accounts, 11 location-weeks) swing an affected location-week by 1–50%, median 12%.

**Statistics**
- Weekly counts are Poisson (Fano ≈ 0.93 at both grains). Spread scales as √λ.
- Use the quasi-Poisson band `λ ± 2.576·√(φλ)`, φ clamped `[1,4]`. **Never a percentage threshold
  or a fixed z-score** — required sensitivity varies ~10× across locations in one account.
- 2.576 is calibrated to ~1 false flag per month for a 15-location account, not picked by
  convention. Changing it changes that rate; see the table in `PLAN.md` §1.
- Baseline = trailing 12 complete weeks, min 8, **excluding detected anomaly weeks**.
- Below λ = 3/week report `not enough volume`, do not flag. 49 of 69 locations average <8/week.

**Fields**

  `connected|missed|voicemail`, appointments → `completed|no_show`, leads → `converted|open`.

# Relay Pulse — DASH-247

Dashboard feature answering "is this activity normal for us?" per account and per location.
Full reasoning in `PLAN.md`. Data evidence in `tools/profile_seed.py`. This file is the
short version: the rules that must hold in code.

## Status

T0–T1 done: skeleton, SQL Server compose, timezone gate green; EF migrations (accounts,
activity_events, `activity_events_dedup` view, week_buckets), seed import, Core bucket generator.
DB counts match the goldens. Review-state table deferred to T5. Next is T2 (aggregation + `/pulse`).

## Stack

| Layer | Choice |
|---|---|
| Backend | .NET 10 Web API, EF Core 10 (migrations — never `EnsureCreated`) |
| DB | SQL Server in Docker |
| Reads | Raw parameterised SQL via `Database.SqlQueryRaw<T>` for the aggregation; EF for writes |
| Frontend | Angular 21 standalone components + signals. **No NgRx** |
| Tests | xUnit; Testcontainers for integration only |
| Tooling | Python 3.10 — `tools/profile_seed.py` (the data oracle) |

## Structure conventions

- **Solution**: `RelayPulse.slnx` with `src/` (Api, Core) and `tests/` (Tests) solution folders. Three
  projects only.
- **Build**: `Directory.Build.props` sets `net10.0`, `Nullable`, `ImplicitUsings`,
  `TreatWarningsAsErrors` once. No per-csproj duplicates, no `LangVersion` pin.
- **Packages**: central management in `Directory.Packages.props`; EF Core / AspNetCore on 10.0.x,
  `Testcontainers.MsSql` for integration. No `Version=` on a `PackageReference`.
- **DI**: each project exposes one `IServiceCollection` extension (`AddCore()`, …) and `Program.cs`
  composes them. `IClock`'s real implementation is registered there and nowhere else.
- **Async**: every async method takes and passes a `CancellationToken`, down to `SqlQueryRaw`.
- **Errors**: 4xx responses are ProblemDetails with a machine-readable code as `title`
  (e.g. `pulse.invalid_week`). 400 for bad parameters only; an empty account is 200, never 404.
- **Logging**: structured message templates with a `Pulse:` prefix
  (`"Pulse: served {AccountId} week {Week}"`) — never string interpolation.
- **Tests**: xUnit v3, plain `Assert` (no FluentAssertions). API tests go through
  `WebApplicationFactory` and assert on the wire JSON via `JsonElement`. Names are
  `Method_Condition_Outcome`. `Program.cs` ends with `public partial class Program;`.
- **Compose**: SQL Server service has a healthcheck; the API `depends_on` it with
  `condition: service_healthy`.

Rejected alternatives (MediatR, extra layers, versioning, Serilog, …) and their reasons are in
`ai-log/decisions.md`. `C:\src\demos\VerusLLC` was a one-time reference for T0 — do not consult it
again; this file is the source of truth.

## Working rules

**Never read `db/seed.sql` in full.** 2.4MB, ~12,600 INSERTs. It will blow out context and tell
you nothing a query won't. To inspect data, run `python tools/profile_seed.py [--dedupe]`, or
load `schema.sql` + `seed.sql` into in-memory SQLite and query it (see `load_db()` in that file).
`head`/`grep` on it is fine.

**Never edit `db/seed.sql` or `db/schema.sql`.** They are the fixture. Dedupe and reshape happen
in migrations and views, never by rewriting the seed.

**No `DateTime.UtcNow` / `DateTime.Now` / `Date.now()` in domain, query, or view code.** Two
separate reasons, both load-bearing:
- *Correctness*: the dataset ends `2026-07-27`, roughly two months before wall clock. Anything
  keyed off the system clock computes an empty current week. The current period comes from
  `MAX(occurred_at)`, not from now.
- *Testability*: golden-value tests must be stable forever.

Inject an `IClock` where a real timestamp is genuinely needed (review-state `created_at`), and
derive every reporting period from the data. A grep for `UtcNow` outside composition root and
clock implementation should return nothing.

**Tests assert golden values produced by `tools/profile_seed.py --dedupe`** — an independent
implementation, in another language, written before any app code. Do not "fix" a failing test by
copying what the C# returned; re-derive from the profiler and find out which one is wrong.

**Unit tests run with zero infrastructure.** Bucketing, bands, verdicts and window completeness
must not need Docker. Integration tests use Testcontainers and skip with a clear message when
Docker is absent, so `dotnet test` is green either way.

**Log decisions in `ai-log/decisions.md`.** Format is at the top of that file: times in
America/Bogota, `time · ACCEPTED|REJECTED|REDIRECTED · what · why · ref`.

## Domain rules

These come from profiling the seed. Violating one produces plausible, wrong numbers.

**Time**
- `occurred_at` is UTC. Bucket in the **account's own IANA timezone**, Mon–Sun weeks.
- Never bucket in UTC. 8 events land in a different week under UTC — small, and exactly the
  regression that will otherwise ship silently.
- Six zones in play, including `America/Phoenix` (no DST) and a literal `UTC`.
- A week is **complete** only when all 7 days fall inside the observation window. Completeness is
  a property of the window, not of where events land — a week with zero events can be complete.
- **Partial weeks are never compared, never used in a baseline, and never the default view.**
  Both edge buckets (`2026-01-26`, `2026-07-27`) cover 1/7 days for all 20 accounts.
- Default view is the **last complete week**: `2026-07-20 … 2026-07-26`.

**Identity**
- Location key is `(account_id, location)`. Labels are generic (`Site A`…`Site O`) and reused
  across accounts — account 1's Site A is not account 6's Site A.
- `accounts.created_at` is **not** the start of history. Every account's events start `2026-02-01`
  regardless. Never window on `created_at`.
- One timezone per account; the schema cannot express per-location zones (known limitation).

**Reads**
- Raw-SQL result rows must not carry `DateTime` unless mapped: the UTC converter reaches
  `SqlQueryRaw<DateTime>` scalars (via `DefaultTypeMapping`) but **not** `DateTime` members of an
  unmapped record — those come back `Unspecified`. Use `DateOnly`/scalars, or map the row type keyless.
- All reporting reads go through the **dedupe view**, never the raw table. 12 exact duplicate rows
  (7 accounts, 11 location-weeks) swing an affected location-week by 1–50%, median 12%.

**Statistics**
- Weekly counts are Poisson (Fano ≈ 0.93 at both grains). Spread scales as √λ.
- Verdicts are **exact Poisson tail tests** (`Core/Statistics`), asymmetric: `below` if
  P(X≤n) < 0.025, `above` if P(X≥n) < 0.005. **Never a percentage threshold or a fixed z-score** —
  required sensitivity varies ~10× across locations in one account. (Supersedes the symmetric
  quasi-Poisson `λ ± 2.576·√(φλ)` band in `PLAN.md` §1; no φ term for now.)
- Band = the integer counts that would be `normal`; it is derived from the same tails, never
  computed separately.
- Baseline = trailing 12 complete weeks, min 8 (else `insufficient_history`), **drop one highest
  and one lowest**, mean of the rest. The trim is what keeps an anomaly out of later baselines.
- Below λ = 3.7/week report `not enough volume`, do not flag. 3.7 sits just above ln 40 = 3.689,
  where an empty week first becomes detectable. 49 of 69 locations average <8/week.
- Rank by `min(p_low/0.025, p_high/0.005)` ascending: < 1 exactly when flagged; unjudged rows get +∞.

**Fields**
- `outcome` is a **per-type** enum, 7 values, not the 5 in `docs/`: calls →
  `connected|missed|voicemail`, appointments → `completed|no_show`, leads → `converted|open`.
- `outcome` NULL is valid (398 rows, 3.2%) — count it, render it as `unspecified`, never drop it.
- `duration_seconds` is noise: calls only, clamped `[20,1500]`, uncorrelated with outcome (missed
  calls median 711s). **Build no metric on it.**
- Hour-of-day is a generator artifact (seed sampled in UTC, never localised). No hour-of-day
  features. Day and week bucketing are unaffected and still required.

**Edge cases that must work**
- Account 20 has zero events → HTTP 200, populated window, `insufficient_history`. Never 404,
  never divide by zero.
- Account 6 week `2026-06-01` is a 12× anomaly of undetermined cause. It must be flagged *and*
  kept out of the next week's baseline by the trim (2026-06-08: λ 72.3, not the plain 138.0).
  Do not "explain" it in code or copy.

## Golden values

From `python tools/profile_seed.py --dedupe`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Events raw → deduped | 12,626 → **12,614** (12 groups, 7 accounts) |
| Buckets per account | 27 total, **25 complete**, last complete `2026-07-20` |
| Account totals, last complete week | 1=**53**, 6=**87**, 8=**7**, 18=**20**, 19=**13**, 20=**0** |
| Account 1 per-location, same week | A=9, B=10, C=9, D=9, E=9, F=7 |
| Account 6 spike week `2026-06-01` | **880** vs λ=72.1 → `above`, all 15 locations `above` |
| Account 6 week after, `2026-06-08` | trimmed λ **72.3** (plain mean 138.0) |
| Bands (λ → normal counts) | 3→[0,8], 6→[2,13], 25→[16,39], 75→[59,98] |
| Dedupe at grain | acct 6 / Site E / `2026-02-23`: 3 → **2** |
| Timezone sensitivity | exactly **8** events change week under UTC bucketing |
| Verdict calibration | acct 8 (7 vs λ=10.4) → `normal`, not a −36% alarm |

## Commands

```bash
python tools/profile_seed.py              # full profile, raw
python tools/profile_seed.py --dedupe     # what the API should serve
python tools/profile_seed.py --markdown   # markdown tables
docker compose up -d                      # SQL Server 2022 on localhost:1433 (see .env.example)
dotnet run --project src/RelayPulse.Api -- seed   # migrate + load db/seed.sql + build week_buckets (idempotent)
dotnet tool restore && dotnet ef migrations add <Name> --project src/RelayPulse.Api --output-dir Data/Migrations
dotnet build && dotnet test               # unit tests need no Docker
```

T2 part 2 is working: the endpoint runs against the seeded database and all 80 tests pass. I recomputed every count and λ on the responses below in Python, independently of the C#, and they all match. Nothing is committed yet.

**Account 1, default week** (`GET /api/accounts/1/pulse`) returns 200. The period is 2026-07-20 … 2026-07-26 with `isDefault: true`, and the state is `ok`.

| row | count | λ | band | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **account** | **53** | 48.0 | [35, 67] | normal |
| Site F | 7 | 8.8 | [4, 17] | normal |
| Site D | 9 | 9.0 | [4, 18] | normal |
| Site E | 9 | 8.5 | [3, 17] | normal |
| Site A | 9 | 7.6 | [3, 16] | normal |
| Site B | 10 | 7.9 | [3, 16] | normal |
| Site C | 9 | 6.5 | [2, 14] | normal |

- The counts match the goldens (53; A=9, B=10, C=9, D=9, E=9, F=7). With nothing flagged, the ranking puts the rows closest to their band edges first.
- The account's calls split as `connected 18, missed 8, voicemail 6, unspecified 2`. Rows with a NULL outcome are counted, not dropped.

**Account 6, spike week** (`GET /api/accounts/6/pulse?week=2026-06-01`) returns 200.
- The account row is **880** against λ = 72.1 (band [56, 95]), verdict **above**.
- All 15 locations are **above**, ranked by how extreme they are. Site C comes first (67 vs λ 3.9, p_high 2e-57) and Site O last (46 vs λ 4.6). The location counts add up to 880.

**Account 20** (`GET /api/accounts/20/pulse`) returns 200 with `"state": "empty"`. The period is filled in, the verdict is `insufficient_history`, every value is null and `locations` is empty.

**Error cases:**
- `week=2026-07-21` (not a Monday), `2026-07-27` and `2026-01-26` (the partial weeks at either end), and `week=junk` all return 400 with title `pulse.invalid_week`. The detail says which Mondays are valid.
- An unknown account returns 404 with title `pulse.account_not_found`.

**Changes made along the way:**
- **`baselineWeeks`** now means the number of prior weeks the baseline actually used, capped at 12. It had been reporting all available weeks (24 for account 20). A new test caught this.
- **Log line:** it now writes the week as `2026-07-20`; before, it printed `07/20/2026` in the machine's local date format.
- **Account 8's golden:** under the trimmed mean its baseline is λ = 10.8, not 10.4. It's still `normal`, and I updated `CLAUDE.md`.
- **`CLAUDE.md`:** the Statistics rules now describe the exact asymmetric tails, the trimmed mean and the 3.7 gate, and I refreshed the goldens and the Status section. `ai-log/decisions.md` has the REDIRECTED entries for all of this.

**Still open:**
- **The log's timestamps look wrong.** I logged my entries at 07:16, the actual time in Bogota. The earlier `11:17`/`11:35` entries match UTC, so they were probably written in UTC but labelled Bogota time. I didn't change them.
- **The endpoint goldens aren't under test.** I verified them live, but there are no integration tests for them yet (Testcontainers plus `WebApplicationFactory`). That's the next piece of T2.
- **Nothing is committed.** Do you want these changes committed as-is, or the integration tests added first?

  I found no blocker-level correctness defects in the statistics, SQL or zero-fill code. The most serious problem is that nothing automatically tests the SQL and the endpoint.
  
  ## Confirmed defects (most severe first)
  
  **1. `tests/RelayPulse.Tests/` (no file) · major · the SQL and the endpoint have no automated tests at all.**
  - **Evidence:** the only test classes are PoissonTail, Baseline, Band, Assess, PulseBuilder, WeekBucketGenerator and TimeZoneResolution. There is no WebApplicationFactory test and no Testcontainers test. CLAUDE.md requires API tests through WebApplicationFactory that assert on the wire JSON.
  - **Failing scenario:** any of these changes would still leave all 80 tests passing:
    - replacing `{RelayDbContext.DedupView}` with `activity_events` in PulseQuery.cs:30;
    - dropping `b.is_complete = 1` (PulseQuery.cs:27);
    - joining on a UTC date instead of `utc_start`/`utc_end`;
    - removing the `JsonStringEnumConverter` (verdicts would go out as integers);
    - returning 404 for account 20.
  - Your live Python cross-check verified this once; nothing guards it from here on.
  - **Fix:** add integration tests (skip when Docker is absent) that assert:
    - acct 1 week 2026-07-20: 53, and A=9 B=10 C=9 D=9 E=9 F=7;
    - acct 6 Site E week 2026-02-23: count 2 (the dedupe golden);
    - acct 20: 200, `"state":"empty"`, `insufficient_history`;
    - `?week=2026-07-27` and `?week=2026-07-21`: 400 with `title` `pulse.invalid_week`;
    - an unknown id: 404 `pulse.account_not_found`;
    - verdicts in snake_case strings.
  
  **2. CLAUDE.md:153-155,158 plus AssessTests.cs:34-37 and BandTests.cs:12 · major (rule 11) · some goldens don't come from the oracle, and one test uses a stale λ.**
  - **Evidence:** the table says it comes "From `python tools/profile_seed.py --dedupe`". A grep of profile_seed.py finds no trimmed mean, no Poisson tail, no alpha values and no bands, and none of 72.1, 72.3 or 10.8. It does print the weekly counts, so the 72.3 fixture in BaselineTests can be re-derived from them by hand. But λ=72.1, the band table and λ=10.8 came from ad-hoc scratchpad scripts that aren't checked in.
  - **Stale test value:** `Assess_Account8SevenAgainst104` and the `[InlineData(10.4, 5, 20)] // account 8's baseline` case use 10.4. That is the old exclude-anomaly baseline from PLAN.md:66/222; the current golden is 10.8. Both tests hard-code λ, so they would pass whatever Baseline computes from acct 8's real series.
  - **Fix:** check in the oracle for tails, bands and the trimmed mean (extend profile_seed.py or add a sibling script), and cite it in the table and the test comments. Relabel 10.4 as a synthetic λ, or change it to 10.8 and derive it from acct 8's weekly counts.
  
  **3. PulseBuilder.cs:34-39 and 42-45 against the PulseReport.cs:12 doc · minor · "empty" and the list of locations are decided from the 13-week fetched slice only.**
  - **Evidence:** `relevant` only holds rows from `[completeWeeks[index-12], target]`, because that is all PulseEndpoints.cs:70-71 fetches. The doc says HasEvents is false only when there are "no events in any complete week up to the target".
  - **Failing scenario:** an account whose last event is more than 13 weeks before the target gets `state:"empty"`, `insufficient_history` and `BaselineWeeks=12`. That contradicts itself: it has 12 weeks of history, all zero, so the result should be λ=0 and `not_enough_volume`. In the same way, a location silent for the whole slice disappears instead of getting a zero-filled row.
  - This can't happen with the seed, since every account and location runs from 2026-02-01.
  - **Fix:** fetch the account's distinct locations, or an existence flag, over all complete weeks up to the target. Otherwise, narrow the doc to "in the baseline window".
  
  **4. PulseEndpoints.cs:55-58 · minor · `completeWeeks.Count == 0` returns 400 `pulse.invalid_week` even when no `week` was sent.**
  - This breaks "400 for bad parameters only". It can't happen with the seed. **Fix:** return 200 with the empty state, or 503, when `requested is null`.
  
  **5. ai-log/decisions.md:43-49 · minor · the new entries are stamped 2026-09-28 07:16 but sit after the 11:35 entries from the same day.**
  - Either these or the earlier entries are not in America/Bogota time as the format requires. **Fix:** correct the timestamps.
  
  ## Checked and found correct
  - **PoissonTail.Lower**
    - The peak index `min(n, ⌊λ⌋)` really is the largest term.
    - `peak` and the loop build their log terms with identical operations, so the peak term comes out as exactly 1.
    - The accumulated log error at λ=500 is around 1e-11 relative.
    - Underflow to 0 (for example Lower(0, 800)) is the right direction.
  - **PoissonTail.Upper, direct-sum branch**
    - It always terminates: since k ≥ n > λ, the ratio λ/(k+1) is always below 1. Terms fall strictly and either drop under the ε test or underflow to 0.
    - It takes at most about 200 iterations at λ≈500, n≈λ.
    - It can't produce NaN.
  - **BandFor**
    - At the top of the lo search range, `Lower(⌈λ⌉, λ)` is at least about 0.5, well above 0.025.
    - The hi search starts at 1, which is right because Upper(0)=1. As λ→0 the band becomes [0,0], and λ=0 gives [0,0].
    - The top of the hi search range, λ+10√λ+20, is well beyond the real crossing for every λ in [0, 500+].
  - **BandFor and Assess cannot disagree.** Both use the same deterministic functions and the same strict comparisons. Below and Above can never both be true, because P(X≤n)+P(X≥n) = 1+P(X=n) ≥ 1.
  - **RankKey.** Flagged rows are below 1, Normal rows are at least 1, and gated or insufficient rows are +∞, so every flagged row ranks above every unflagged one.
  - **SQL**
    - It is parameterised, and the only interpolation is a `const` view name.
    - It reads the dedupe view and range-joins on the account timezone's `[utc_start, utc_end)`.
    - It filters to complete weeks and uses DateOnly for the week (no DateTime in the result row).
    - GROUPING SETS can't double-count: `location` is NOT NULL (schema.sql:17), so NULL only marks account-grain rows, and C# splits the two grains on that.
  - **Window edges**
    - A target on the first complete week gives no prior weeks, `insufficient_history` and a null PreviousWeek.
    - The 13-week fetch exactly covers the 12 prior weeks that Baseline uses. The zero-filled weeks before `from` are never read, because Lambda only takes the last 12.
    - Partial weeks and weeks after the target are filtered out in both SQL and C#.
  - **Conventions:** no wall clock is used; the CancellationToken reaches `ToListAsync`; the log template is structured; ProblemDetails titles are codes; locations are keyed by account because every query is scoped to one account.
  
  ## Judgement calls (not defects)
  - **Band on gated rows (Significance.cs:42-46):** at λ=3.0 with count 12, the row shows band [0,8] but the verdict is `not_enough_volume`. The UI will show a count outside the "normal" range with no flag, while the spec defines the band as counts that would not be flagged. Consider a null band for gated rows, or label the band clearly.
  - **Ties when p underflows (PoissonTail.cs:77):** `Upper(880, 72.3)` returns exactly 0, so RankKey is 0. Several extreme flags would then be ordered by name, not by how extreme they are. Ranking on log p would fix this. It has little effect with the seed.
  - **Coupling between Builder and endpoint:** PulseBuilder zero-fills any prior week it has no rows for. That is only right because the endpoint fetches exactly `index-12..index`. A future change to the fetch window would silently produce zero baselines. An assertion or a comment on `Build` would guard this.
  - **Weak tail tests:** `LowerAndUpper_AdjacentCounts_SumToOne` (PoissonTailTests.cs:58-65) checks to 1e-12 absolute, which can't detect relative errors in tails far below 1e-12. Only one far-upper-tail reference point exists (600 at λ=500). Consider adding reference values such as Upper(60, 20) and Lower(0, 500).
  - **Explicit grain marker:** `GROUPING(e.location) AS IsAccountGrain` would make the grain explicit instead of relying on the NOT NULL column. It is not needed today.

The reviewer found no correctness bugs in the statistics, the SQL or the zero-fill. Its main findings are about verification: nothing automatically guards the SQL or the endpoint, and some of the goldens I added don't come from a checked-in source. I haven't changed anything yet.

**Real problems:**

1. **The SQL and the endpoint have no automated tests.** All 80 tests would still pass if the query read the raw table instead of the dedupe view, or dropped `is_complete = 1`, or if verdicts went out as numbers, or if account 20 returned 404. My live cross-check verified these once; nothing protects them from here on. Fixing this means the Testcontainers + `WebApplicationFactory` tests I'd already listed as outstanding. The reviewer also suggests adding the Site E dedupe golden (2026-02-23 → 2) and a snake_case verdict check to them.
2. **Some of the goldens I added don't come from the oracle.** The `CLAUDE.md` table says its values come from `profile_seed.py --dedupe`, but λ=72.1, λ=10.8 and the band values came from throwaway scripts in my scratchpad. The reviewer is right, and it breaks the project's own rule. Two tests also still use account 8's old λ of 10.4 while labelling it "account 8's baseline". They pass anyway, because they hard-code λ rather than computing it from account 8's weekly counts.
   - Fix: check in the oracle for Poisson tails, bands and the trimmed mean (extend `profile_seed.py` or add a companion script) and cite it. Then relabel 10.4 as a synthetic λ, or change it to 10.8 and derive it from account 8's real weekly counts.
3. **"Empty" is decided from the 13 weeks fetched, not the whole history.** An account whose last event was more than 13 weeks before the chosen week would show `empty` / `insufficient_history`, when it should be `not_enough_volume` with λ=0. A location that was silent for those 13 weeks disappears instead of getting a zero row. This can't happen with the seed, but the code's doc comment claims the whole history. Fix it by fetching the account's list of locations across all complete weeks, or narrow the doc.
4. **With no week requested and no complete weeks in the database, the endpoint returns 400.** That breaks "400 for bad parameters only"; it should be a 200 empty state. It can't happen with the seed.
5. **The `decisions.md` timestamps don't agree.** This is the clock mismatch I raised last turn. You'll need to decide which entries are in the wrong timezone.

**Worth deciding, but not defects:**
- **Band on low-volume rows:** they still show a band. At λ=3, a count of 12 is outside [0, 8] but isn't flagged, which will look inconsistent in the UI. I'd return a null band when the verdict is `not_enough_volume`.
- **Ties among extreme flags:** very extreme p-values round to exactly 0, so several flagged rows can tie and fall back to name order. Ranking on log p fixes it; with the seed it hardly matters.
- **Coupling between the builder and the endpoint:** the builder treats any missing prior week as zero. That's only right because the endpoint fetches exactly the 12 weeks before the chosen one, so a comment or check should guard it.
- **Tail tests:** they only check to 1e-12 absolute and have one far-tail reference value. More reference points (such as `Upper(60, 20)` and `Lower(0, 500)`) would strengthen them.

The reviewer also confirmed as correct: every tail sum terminates and can't produce NaN; the band and the verdict can never disagree; flagged rows always rank above unflagged ones; the two SQL grains can't double-count; and the window edges behave.

I'd fix 2, 3 and 4 plus the null band now, since they're small, then write the integration tests for 1 before committing. For 5, tell me which set of timestamps is wrong and I'll correct it. Shall I go ahead?

# Relay Pulse — DASH-247

Dashboard feature answering "is this activity normal for us?" per account and per location.
Full reasoning in `PLAN.md`. Data evidence in `tools/profile_seed.py`. This file is the
short version: the rules that must hold in code.

## Status

T0–T1 done: skeleton, SQL Server compose, timezone gate green; EF migrations (accounts,
activity_events, `activity_events_dedup` view, week_buckets), seed import, Core bucket generator.
DB counts match the goldens. Review-state table deferred to T5.
T2 in progress: Core statistics + `PulseBuilder` (unit-tested), `GET /api/accounts/{id}/pulse`
live and cross-checked against the oracle for accts 1, 6, 20. Missing: Testcontainers
integration tests for the endpoint goldens.

## Stack

| Layer | Choice |
|---|---|
| Backend | .NET 10 Web API, EF Core 10 (migrations — never `EnsureCreated`) |
| DB | SQL Server in Docker |
| Reads | Raw parameterised SQL via `Database.SqlQueryRaw<T>` for the aggregation; EF for writes |
| Frontend | Angular 21 standalone components + signals. **No NgRx** |
| Tests | xUnit; Testcontainers for integration only |
| Tooling | Python 3.10 — `tools/profile_seed.py` (the data oracle) |

## Structure conventions

- **Solution**: `RelayPulse.slnx` with `src/` (Api, Core) and `tests/` (Tests) solution folders. Three
  projects only.
- **Build**: `Directory.Build.props` sets `net10.0`, `Nullable`, `ImplicitUsings`,
  `TreatWarningsAsErrors` once. No per-csproj duplicates, no `LangVersion` pin.
- **Packages**: central management in `Directory.Packages.props`; EF Core / AspNetCore on 10.0.x,
  `Testcontainers.MsSql` for integration. No `Version=` on a `PackageReference`.
- **DI**: each project exposes one `IServiceCollection` extension (`AddCore()`, …) and `Program.cs`
  composes them. `IClock`'s real implementation is registered there and nowhere else.
- **Async**: every async method takes and passes a `CancellationToken`, down to `SqlQueryRaw`.
- **Errors**: 4xx responses are ProblemDetails with a machine-readable code as `title`
  (e.g. `pulse.invalid_week`). 400 for bad parameters only; an empty account is 200, never 404.
- **Logging**: structured message templates with a `Pulse:` prefix
  (`"Pulse: served {AccountId} week {Week}"`) — never string interpolation.
- **Tests**: xUnit v3, plain `Assert` (no FluentAssertions). API tests go through
  `WebApplicationFactory` and assert on the wire JSON via `JsonElement`. Names are
  `Method_Condition_Outcome`. `Program.cs` ends with `public partial class Program;`.
- **Compose**: SQL Server service has a healthcheck; the API `depends_on` it with
  `condition: service_healthy`.

Rejected alternatives (MediatR, extra layers, versioning, Serilog, …) and their reasons are in
`ai-log/decisions.md`. `C:\src\demos\VerusLLC` was a one-time reference for T0 — do not consult it
again; this file is the source of truth.

## Working rules

**Never read `db/seed.sql` in full.** 2.4MB, ~12,600 INSERTs. It will blow out context and tell
you nothing a query won't. To inspect data, run `python tools/profile_seed.py [--dedupe]`, or
load `schema.sql` + `seed.sql` into in-memory SQLite and query it (see `load_db()` in that file).
`head`/`grep` on it is fine.

**Never edit `db/seed.sql` or `db/schema.sql`.** They are the fixture. Dedupe and reshape happen
in migrations and views, never by rewriting the seed.

**No `DateTime.UtcNow` / `DateTime.Now` / `Date.now()` in domain, query, or view code.** Two
separate reasons, both load-bearing:
- *Correctness*: the dataset ends `2026-07-27`, roughly two months before wall clock. Anything
  keyed off the system clock computes an empty current week. The current period comes from
  `MAX(occurred_at)`, not from now.
- *Testability*: golden-value tests must be stable forever.

Inject an `IClock` where a real timestamp is genuinely needed (review-state `created_at`), and
derive every reporting period from the data. A grep for `UtcNow` outside composition root and
clock implementation should return nothing.

**Tests assert golden values produced by `tools/profile_seed.py --dedupe`** — an independent
implementation, in another language, written before any app code. Do not "fix" a failing test by
copying what the C# returned; re-derive from the profiler and find out which one is wrong.

**Unit tests run with zero infrastructure.** Bucketing, bands, verdicts and window completeness
must not need Docker. Integration tests use Testcontainers and skip with a clear message when
Docker is absent, so `dotnet test` is green either way.

**Log decisions in `ai-log/decisions.md`.** Format is at the top of that file: times in
America/Bogota, `time · ACCEPTED|REJECTED|REDIRECTED · what · why · ref`.

## Domain rules

These come from profiling the seed. Violating one produces plausible, wrong numbers.

**Time**
- `occurred_at` is UTC. Bucket in the **account's own IANA timezone**, Mon–Sun weeks.
- Never bucket in UTC. 8 events land in a different week under UTC — small, and exactly the
  regression that will otherwise ship silently.
- Six zones in play, including `America/Phoenix` (no DST) and a literal `UTC`.
- A week is **complete** only when all 7 days fall inside the observation window. Completeness is
  a property of the window, not of where events land — a week with zero events can be complete.
- **Partial weeks are never compared, never used in a baseline, and never the default view.**
  Both edge buckets (`2026-01-26`, `2026-07-27`) cover 1/7 days for all 20 accounts.
- Default view is the **last complete week**: `2026-07-20 … 2026-07-26`.

**Identity**
- Location key is `(account_id, location)`. Labels are generic (`Site A`…`Site O`) and reused
  across accounts — account 1's Site A is not account 6's Site A.
- `accounts.created_at` is **not** the start of history. Every account's events start `2026-02-01`
  regardless. Never window on `created_at`.
- One timezone per account; the schema cannot express per-location zones (known limitation).

**Reads**
- Raw-SQL result rows must not carry `DateTime` unless mapped: the UTC converter reaches
  `SqlQueryRaw<DateTime>` scalars (via `DefaultTypeMapping`) but **not** `DateTime` members of an
  unmapped record — those come back `Unspecified`. Use `DateOnly`/scalars, or map the row type keyless.
- All reporting reads go through the **dedupe view**, never the raw table. 12 exact duplicate rows
  (7 accounts, 11 location-weeks) swing an affected location-week by 1–50%, median 12%.

**Statistics**
- Weekly counts are Poisson (Fano ≈ 0.93 at both grains). Spread scales as √λ.
- Verdicts are **exact Poisson tail tests** (`Core/Statistics`), asymmetric: `below` if
  P(X≤n) < 0.025, `above` if P(X≥n) < 0.005. **Never a percentage threshold or a fixed z-score** —
  required sensitivity varies ~10× across locations in one account. (Supersedes the symmetric
  quasi-Poisson `λ ± 2.576·√(φλ)` band in `PLAN.md` §1; no φ term for now.)
- Band = the integer counts that would be `normal`; it is derived from the same tails, never
  computed separately.
- Baseline = trailing 12 complete weeks, min 8 (else `insufficient_history`), **drop one highest
  and one lowest**, mean of the rest. The trim is what keeps an anomaly out of later baselines.
- Below λ = 3.7/week report `not enough volume`, do not flag. 3.7 sits just above ln 40 = 3.689,
  where an empty week first becomes detectable. 49 of 69 locations average <8/week.
- Rank by `min(p_low/0.025, p_high/0.005)` ascending: < 1 exactly when flagged; unjudged rows get +∞.

**Fields**
- `outcome` is a **per-type** enum, 7 values, not the 5 in `docs/`: calls →
  `connected|missed|voicemail`, appointments → `completed|no_show`, leads → `converted|open`.
- `outcome` NULL is valid (398 rows, 3.2%) — count it, render it as `unspecified`, never drop it.
- `duration_seconds` is noise: calls only, clamped `[20,1500]`, uncorrelated with outcome (missed
  calls median 711s). **Build no metric on it.**
- Hour-of-day is a generator artifact (seed sampled in UTC, never localised). No hour-of-day
  features. Day and week bucketing are unaffected and still required.

**Edge cases that must work**
- Account 20 has zero events → HTTP 200, populated window, `insufficient_history`. Never 404,
  never divide by zero.
- Account 6 week `2026-06-01` is a 12× anomaly of undetermined cause. It must be flagged *and*
  kept out of the next week's baseline by the trim (2026-06-08: λ 72.3, not the plain 138.0).
  Do not "explain" it in code or copy.

## Golden values

From `python tools/profile_seed.py --dedupe`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Events raw → deduped | 12,626 → **12,614** (12 groups, 7 accounts) |
| Buckets per account | 27 total, **25 complete**, last complete `2026-07-20` |
| Account totals, last complete week | 1=**53**, 6=**87**, 8=**7**, 18=**20**, 19=**13**, 20=**0** |
| Account 1 per-location, same week | A=9, B=10, C=9, D=9, E=9, F=7 |
| Account 6 spike week `2026-06-01` | **880** vs λ=72.1 → `above`, all 15 locations `above` |
| Account 6 week after, `2026-06-08` | trimmed λ **72.3** (plain mean 138.0) |
| Bands (λ → normal counts) | 3→[0,8], 6→[2,13], 25→[16,39], 75→[59,98] |
| Dedupe at grain | acct 6 / Site E / `2026-02-23`: 3 → **2** |
| Timezone sensitivity | exactly **8** events change week under UTC bucketing |
| Verdict calibration | acct 8 (7 vs λ=10.8) → `normal`, not a −36% alarm |

## Commands

```bash
python tools/profile_seed.py              # full profile, raw
python tools/profile_seed.py --dedupe     # what the API should serve
python tools/profile_seed.py --markdown   # markdown tables
docker compose up -d                      # SQL Server 2022 on localhost:1433 (see .env.example)
dotnet run --project src/RelayPulse.Api -- seed   # migrate + load db/seed.sql + build week_buckets (idempotent)
dotnet tool restore && dotnet ef migrations add <Name> --project src/RelayPulse.Api --output-dir Data/Migrations
dotnet build && dotnet test               # unit tests need no Docker
```

message.content:
Go ahead, with this scope:
- Fix 2: extend tools/profile_seed.py (or add tools/oracle_poisson.py) to compute Poisson tails,
  bands, trimmed-mean λ and the verdict from seed data, and cite it as the source of every
  golden. Use λ=10.8 derived from account 8's real weekly counts; if a test needs a synthetic λ,
  label it synthetic. Add Upper(60,20) and Lower(0,500) as reference points, values from the oracle.
- Fix 3: build the location list from all complete weeks up to the selected week, so a location
  silent for 13+ weeks still gets zero rows.
- Fix 4: no complete weeks → 200 empty state, not 400.
- Null band when verdict is not_enough_volume.
- Add a guard/comment for the builder's "missing prior week = 0" assumption.
- Defer: log-p tie-breaking (note it for the README).
- Do NOT write integration tests now. That's T3, in the next session.
Run all tests, show me the result, then stop so I can commit T2.

Timestamps in decisions.md: everything must be America/Bogota (UTC-5). Convert any line
written in UTC by subtracting 5h, and check against `git log --date=local`. Show me the diff.

-Full reasoning in `PLAN.md`. Data evidence in `tools/profile_seed.py`. This file is the
-short version: the rules that must hold in code.

-| Backend | .NET 10 Web API, EF Core 10 (migrations — never `EnsureCreated`) |
-| Reads | Raw parameterised SQL via `Database.SqlQueryRaw<T>` for the aggregation; EF for writes |
-| Frontend | Angular 21 standalone components + signals. **No NgRx** |
-| Tests | xUnit; Testcontainers for integration only |
-- **Solution**: `RelayPulse.slnx` with `src/` (Api, Core) and `tests/` (Tests) solution folders. Three
-  `TreatWarningsAsErrors` once. No per-csproj duplicates, no `LangVersion` pin.
-- **Packages**: central management in `Directory.Packages.props`; EF Core / AspNetCore on 10.0.x,
-- **DI**: each project exposes one `IServiceCollection` extension (`AddCore()`, …) and `Program.cs`
-  composes them. `IClock`'s real implementation is registered there and nowhere else.
-- **Async**: every async method takes and passes a `CancellationToken`, down to `SqlQueryRaw`.
-- **Errors**: 4xx responses are ProblemDetails with a machine-readable code as `title`
-  (e.g. `pulse.invalid_week`). 400 for bad parameters only; an empty account is 200, never 404.
-- **Logging**: structured message templates with a `Pulse:` prefix
-- **Tests**: xUnit v3, plain `Assert` (no FluentAssertions). API tests go through
-  `WebApplicationFactory` and assert on the wire JSON via `JsonElement`. Names are
-- **Compose**: SQL Server service has a healthcheck; the API `depends_on` it with

-again; this file is the source of truth.

-you nothing a query won't. To inspect data, run `python tools/profile_seed.py [--dedupe]`, or
-load `schema.sql` + `seed.sql` into in-memory SQLite and query it (see `load_db()` in that file).
-**Never edit `db/seed.sql` or `db/schema.sql`.** They are the fixture. Dedupe and reshape happen
-in migrations and views, never by rewriting the seed.
-**No `DateTime.UtcNow` / `DateTime.Now` / `Date.now()` in domain, query, or view code.** Two
-- *Correctness*: the dataset ends `2026-07-27`, roughly two months before wall clock. Anything

-- *Testability*: golden-value tests must be stable forever.

-**Tests assert golden values produced by `tools/profile_seed.py --dedupe`** — an independent

-**Log decisions in `ai-log/decisions.md`.** Format is at the top of that file: times in
-These come from profiling the seed. Violating one produces plausible, wrong numbers.
-- `occurred_at` is UTC. Bucket in the **account's own IANA timezone**, Mon–Sun weeks.
-- Never bucket in UTC. 8 events land in a different week under UTC — small, and exactly the
-  regression that will otherwise ship silently.
-- Six zones in play, including `America/Phoenix` (no DST) and a literal `UTC`.
-- A week is **complete** only when all 7 days fall inside the observation window. Completeness is
-  a property of the window, not of where events land — a week with zero events can be complete.
-- **Partial weeks are never compared, never used in a baseline, and never the default view.**
-  Both edge buckets (`2026-01-26`, `2026-07-27`) cover 1/7 days for all 20 accounts.
-- Default view is the **last complete week**: `2026-07-20 … 2026-07-26`.
-- Location key is `(account_id, location)`. Labels are generic (`Site A`…`Site O`) and reused
-  across accounts — account 1's Site A is not account 6's Site A.
-- `accounts.created_at` is **not** the start of history. Every account's events start `2026-02-01`
-- One timezone per account; the schema cannot express per-location zones (known limitation).
-- Raw-SQL result rows must not carry `DateTime` unless mapped: the UTC converter reaches
-  unmapped record — those come back `Unspecified`. Use `DateOnly`/scalars, or map the row type keyless.
-- All reporting reads go through the **dedupe view**, never the raw table. 12 exact duplicate rows
-  (7 accounts, 11 location-weeks) swing an affected location-week by 1–50%, median 12%.
-- Weekly counts are Poisson (Fano ≈ 0.93 at both grains). Spread scales as √λ.
-- Verdicts are **exact Poisson tail tests** (`Core/Statistics`), asymmetric: `below` if
-  P(X≤n) < 0.025, `above` if P(X≥n) < 0.005. **Never a percentage threshold or a fixed z-score** —
-  required sensitivity varies ~10× across locations in one account. (Supersedes the symmetric
-  quasi-Poisson `λ ± 2.576·√(φλ)` band in `PLAN.md` §1; no φ term for now.)
-- Band = the integer counts that would be `normal`; it is derived from the same tails, never
-- Baseline = trailing 12 complete weeks, min 8 (else `insufficient_history`), **drop one highest
-  and one lowest**, mean of the rest. The trim is what keeps an anomaly out of later baselines.
-- Below λ = 3.7/week report `not enough volume`, do not flag. 3.7 sits just above ln 40 = 3.689,
-  where an empty week first becomes detectable. 49 of 69 locations average <8/week.

**What changed against your scope:**
- **Fix 2:**
  - I renamed my oracle to `tools/oracle_poisson.py`. It now prints every value the tests use: the reference tails, including `P(X≥60 | λ=20) = 4.233e-13` and `P(X≤0 | λ=500) = 7.125e-218`; the bands; and the real weekly series behind account 6's baseline (72.3) and account 8's (10.8).
  - Account 8's λ is computed from its real weekly counts.
  - Every λ in the tests is labelled either synthetic or real.
  - Labelling exposed a mistake of mine: two tests paired the spike count 880 with λ = 72.3, which is the *following* week's baseline. They now use 72.1, week 2026-06-01's own baseline. The verdict is still `above`.
- **Fix 3:** the endpoint now fetches every complete week up to the selected one, so a location silent for 13+ weeks still gets a row. A builder test covers this case.
- **Fix 4:** when there are no complete weeks and no week was requested, the endpoint returns 200 with the empty state.
- **Null band:** `not_enough_volume` rows no longer carry a band.
- **Zero-fill guard:** there is a comment at the zero-fill line and the contract is stated in `Build`'s docs. It's documentation only; the builder can't tell "not fetched" apart from "no events" at runtime.
